extracted.intended_audience: general readers and journalism professionals interested in local news, media ethics, and AI in newsrooms
extracted.subtask_description: A journalistic report documenting an instance where an AI company produced local news content that copied reporting and photography from local outlets, highlighting ethical, legal, and editorial failings. The page illustrates standards and failings relevant to using AI in local journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and credit to original journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories included reporting, writing and photography from local journalists without attribution; 'It would be nice for any outlet … to give credit where credit is due.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always credit the original reporter or outlet when using their reporting or materials. Avoid removing or omitting references to original outlets; do not republish others' work as your own. Examples/anti-patterns: Nota News removed references to original outlets, presented others' work under its own bylines, and republished quotes without credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only public civic information for AI-generated civic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles were supposed to be based on publicly available civic information, such as press releases and videos of city council meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When generating reporting via AI, limit sourcing to verifiable public civic records and original reporting rather than repurposing other news outlets' coverage. Anti-pattern: running other outlets' articles through AI to produce derivative pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear editorial guidelines and documented newsroom rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Nota News 'was not a traditional newsroom environment' and 'lacked clear editorial guidelines' — 'They don’t have anything on paper. They don’t have rules. They don’t have manuals.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain written editorial policies, style guides, and procedures (e.g., sourcing, attribution, image use, fact-checking) and ensure contractors/staff are trained on them. Absence of documentation is an editorial failure; examples: journalists worked with no editors checking work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior leadership oversight and enforceable guardrails
rubrics_metrics.description: Nota said it would 'implement stricter guardrails and more oversight from senior leadership.' Brandau described failure of contractor journalists to follow standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure senior leaders set, monitor, and enforce editorial standards for AI-generated content; provide oversight rather than leaving contractors to self-police. Anti-pattern: delegating to contractors with minimal supervision and no escalation path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about AI use and how AI is applied
rubrics_metrics.description: All Nota News pages noted they were 'Powered by Nota News and Springwire.ai.' None, however, disclosed how the sites used AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly disclose whether and how AI models are used (generation, summarization, translation, training data), including limitations and potential errors. Avoid opaque 'powered by' labels without explanation. Example: disclosure should state whether content is human-edited, auto-generated, or an experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright compliance for text and images
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyright law protects original works of authorship... Creating a digital copy of something is considered tangible form... Poynter identified more than 30 images on Nota News that were copied from other sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain rights or permission for republished text and photos, or properly license/attribute images; do not reproduce copyrighted content without authorization. Legal test: amount taken and purpose matter for text; photographs are 'much more clear-cut' and require rights clearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct attribution and treatment of quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: When copying quotes from other news sites, Nota News typically removed references to the original outlet; in some cases paraphrased material was still presented in quotation marks or quotation marks were added where none existed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute quotes to their original sources and avoid presenting paraphrases as verbatim quotes. Do not alter quote attribution or punctuation in ways that misrepresent the original. Anti-patterns: paraphrasing then enclosing in quotes, removing attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous fact-checking and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: A properly reported and fact-checked article... can cost hundreds or thousands of dollars; Nota's model producing stories for less than $10 wouldn't allow time for fact-checking or watching long recordings to verify accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate time and resources for verification (e.g., confirm sources, check records, view meeting recordings) before publishing. Do not prioritize speed/volume over verification. Example failure: publishing a story about a bill two years late and with misleading context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve timeliness and accuracy of context
rubrics_metrics.description: One Nota News story reported that the Utah state legislature had passed a bill 'two years after it actually passed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reporting accurately reflects timing and current status of events and laws; verify dates and whether developments remain relevant. Avoid republishing outdated coverage as new reporting without context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid prioritizing quantity over quality (reasonable quotas)
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal was to produce 10 to 15 stories a day. Nota leadership emphasized quantity over quality. Rodríguez said he was given a quota that was impossible to meet using traditional journalistic techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set realistic production expectations that permit proper sourcing, verification, and editing. High quotas that incentivize shortcutting (copying, not verifying) are an editorial anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility of individual journalists and contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Rodríguez: 'That context does not remove my responsibility. As a journalist, I should have applied my own standards regardless of the environment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors and journalists must adhere to journalistic ethics and standards even within experimental projects; organizations should make expectations explicit and hold individuals accountable. Anti-pattern: treating the work as non-journalistic to justify lax standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper use and configuration of AI models (data retention and hallucination management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brandau said the tools used were not set to retain any information submitted; he said Polaris was trained on 'rights-cleared data' and on open-source models against each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configure AI systems to avoid unintended retention of proprietary or scraped content; document training data sources and techniques; implement methods to reduce hallucinations and factual errors. Anti-patterns: using models without controls or clarity about retention/training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training-data transparency and client consent for model training
rubrics_metrics.description: While Nota does not train its models on its customers' data by default, some clients chose to grant permission... The copying of client content raises questions about how those standards were applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent with customers about whether their content is used to train models and obtain informed consent; keep records of permissions. Avoid ambiguity that could lead to customer content being reused without clear authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights-cleared images and explicit image sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Poynter found more than 30 images on Nota News that were copied from other sites; questions about how photos were sourced and credited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only licensed or rights-cleared images, and include clear photo credits. If images are derived or processed by AI, disclose provenance and licensing. Anti-pattern: copying outlet photos without permission or credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent experimental labeling and access control
rubrics_metrics.description: Brandau said the sites were 'live experiments' and 'were never meant to be public' but the company issued a press release listing the URLs and the sites were discoverable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If content is experimental, clearly label it as such and restrict public indexing/access until it's ready; avoid presenting experiments as finished public journalism. Anti-pattern: promoting experiments publicly while claiming they are internal demos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate and culturally competent bilingual publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories were published in both English and Spanish; to create Spanish versions an editor 'used Google Translate.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure bilingual content is produced or reviewed by proficient human translators/editors to maintain accuracy, nuance, and cultural context. Avoid relying solely on machine translation for published bilingual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of press releases and attribution to official sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Poynter also found multiple cases where Nota News took content from press releases without attribution and added errors likely generated by AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using press releases, clearly attribute them and verify claims; do not republish press-release language as independent reporting without context or fact-checking. Anti-pattern: treating press releases as finished reporting without verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in names, terms, and factual details
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of errors introduced: 'Georgia O’Keeffe' shortened to 'Ga. O’Keeffe'; 'K-9' spelled 'K-nine.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully proofread for correct spelling of names, terms, and technical details; do not allow automated processes to introduce awkward abbreviations or incorrect forms. Such errors undermine credibility and indicate insufficient editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not republish client or partner content without consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of Nota’s clients were among the outlets whose work appeared on Nota News; Community Journals and Nexstar content showed up on Nota News without their prior awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never republish or repurpose client/partner content for public-facing sites without explicit permission and clear contractual terms. Anti-pattern: reusing client-produced journalism internally or in experiments that become public without consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenue/monetization transparency for experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: One Nota News site included a page inviting readers to contribute money; Brandau said Nota did not receive any money, but the presence of donation widgets suggested potential monetization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent if experimental content solicits payments or donations; do not present experimental/demo sites with donation options unless funds, data handling, and obligations are clearly disclosed. Anti-pattern: exposing donation forms on demos without clear accounting.
